description: GRAIN: logical module (class / VB module), plus the data store, the Access file and the one external target as terminal nodes. Node ids for the six code modules match structural-analysis.json `modules[].id` exactly, so the two documents compose. This grain was chosen because the application has only one build module and one deployment surface — a project-reference graph would be a single node and say nothing, while a method-level graph over 461 hand-written lines would be noise. Edge count is small by nature: 9 code-to-code edges, 7 code-to-data edges, 1 outbound. What matters in this graph is not its size but that 3 of the 9 code-to-code edges are cycle members, and that 4 independent modules converge on one shared mutable connection object.

notes:
WHAT THIS TRAVERSAL COULD NOT RESOLVE, stated so the graph is not read as complete:

1. DEFAULT-INSTANCE TARGETS ARE AMBIGUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION. Five edges are VB default-instance calls (`Form1.LoadData()`, `ViewForm.LoadData()`, `Form1.Panel5`). Statically these resolve to the generated My.Forms singletons; at runtime the forms the user actually sees are separate objects created with `New` in Form1 and ViewForm. Both readings are defensible and they disagree, so each such edge is marked `resolves_to_displayed_instance: false` rather than silently picked. This is the application's most consequential structural defect and it is invisible to any tool that resolves these names statically and stops there.

2. EVENT-HANDLER EDGES ARE NOT MODELLED INDIVIDUALLY. WinForms `Handles` clauses and the one dynamic `AddHandler editForm.FormClosed` (ViewForm.vb:75) are UI-framework dispatch, folded into the module-grain edges above. The AddHandler is never removed, so a reused EditForm accumulates subscriptions — a multiplicity the graph cannot express at this grain.

3. 2,326 OF 2,787 LINES ARE DESIGNER-GENERATED LAYOUT and contribute no call edges, only control construction. They are counted in each node's `loc` because they are real maintenance surface — Form1.Designer.vb alone is 1,211 lines and 77 controls — but they are deliberately not traversed for edges.

4. THE DATABASE CONTRIBUTES NO EDGES OF ITS OWN. Confirmed by decoding the .accdb catalog directly: zero stored procedures, zero views, zero triggers, zero relationships, zero database links. Every edge touching `db.students` therefore originates in application code — unusually for a legacy application, there is no logic hiding in the database. That is a measured finding, not an unexamined assumption.

5. NO REFLECTION, NO LATE-BOUND DISPATCH AND NO GENERATED CODE PATHS were found, so there are no hidden call edges of that kind. But OptionStrict is Off project-wide (vbproj:51) and column access is by string name (`stReader("fname")`, `Cells("rollno")`), so the application's data contract — as opposed to its call graph — is resolved at runtime and is not verifiable from source.

6. NO BUILD WAS PERFORMED. A clean clone does not build (manifest signing against a gitignored, absent .pfx) and could not connect if it did (the hardcoded D:\PROGRAMING path does not exist in the repository layout), so no edge here is confirmed by execution or by a compiler. Every edge is cited to a file and line a reader can check instead.
